justification: Title-only record: title makes KG subgraph exploration over prior reasoning paths the mechanism, so search shape; an ESWA full paper reporting such a framework is a lab-validated technique.
Title-only: 'Iterative Self-Refined' names the revise-on-feedback step as the contribution, applied to planning; an ICRA paper reports simulated planning-domain results, i.e. lab validation.
Title-only: 'Iterative Semantic Refinement' is a VLM-driven refine-on-feedback loop for editing; short symposium record shows no evidence beyond a proposed approach with worked edits.
Title-only: an empirical audit of one named mechanism, self-reflection, so it codes to that mechanism; 'Effects on Problem-Solving Performance' means reflection conditions compared in the lab.

Abstract's ablation credits 'the dynamic feedback iterative mechanism', the extraction-verification-feedback-optimization rewrite, not the agent arrangement; evidence is DuIE 2.0 scores, a lab benchmark.
Title-only: 'closed-loop feedback framework for iterative optimization' names the revision loop as the contribution; the symposium record gives no evidence of a validation beyond the proposal.
Title-only: 'Iterative Self-Correction' is the contributed revise step for re-ID with LVLMs; an ACL Findings paper reports scores on standard re-ID datasets, so lab validation.

Contribution is an instrument: a 'multi-criteria evaluation methodology' with formulations quantifying self-correction and consistency; evidence is 'extensive empirical analysis across diverse datasets' in the lab.
Title-only: SWRV contributes step-wise self-verification, i.e. how the judgement on each step is produced; an XLLM25 shared-task system paper is scored on the task data, so lab validation.

Its object is reasoning effort and disengagement under load, 'reduction in reasoning effort' and computational 'rest' periods, i.e. how much the loop spends; it reframes via dual-process theory and only proposes hypotheses.

Contribution is 'modular refiner policies' driving an inference-time iterative refinement process, the correction step; the paper only proposes and argues for the architecture, with analysis and discussion, no study.
Title-only: GraphReason's contribution is a graph-based verification approach, the judgement over candidate reasoning chains; an ACL workshop paper reports reasoning-benchmark accuracy in the lab.

RPR-RAG 'incrementally builds a subgraph' and extracts reasoning paths, changing the shape of exploration (runner-up: budget, via the stopping criterion); results are WebQSP, CWQ and MetaQA scores in the lab.

Novelty is how the step judgement is produced: process-supervision data for validity prediction, verification as 'process-level control signal' (runner-up: critique_and_revision); evidence is lab scores vs ReFT and Lumos.
Title-only: the contribution is a verifier over knowledge-augmented generations, a check on outputs; an EMNLP main-conference paper reports benchmark accuracy in the lab.
Title-only: Critic-CoT's contribution is chain-of-thought critique fed back to correct the attempt, the revision step; an ACL Findings paper reports reasoning-benchmark gains in the lab.
Title-only: CriticEval is an instrument, a benchmark for measuring critique ability, not a loop mechanism; a NeurIPS dataset paper scores existing models on it in the lab.

Contribution is a diagnostic instrument: Wordle 'as a diagnostic testbed' with convergence-efficiency measures; 5,400+ runs per configuration against VOI, CSS and random baselines in a controlled setting.
Title-only: 'Iterative Informed Navigation' over a knowledge graph is candidate expansion and selection, the exploration shape; a KDD paper reports KGQA benchmark results in the lab.
Title-only: IVC-DB's novelty is how the check is produced, dual-backward mathematical verification of the answer; a Knowledge-Based Systems paper reports math-benchmark accuracy in the lab.

Title-only: the mechanism is uncertainty-guided verification, a confidence signal gating the answer (runner-up: budget, via adaptive test-time compute); a CICSE paper reports reasoning-benchmark results in the lab.

Title-only: 'Adaptive Verification' is the contribution, deciding when a reasoning chain must be checked before it stands (runner-up: budget control); an ACL Findings paper reports benchmark accuracy in the lab.

The contribution is the arrangement itself: a shared task-ledger protocol, dependency-aware task graph and role-isolated agents; evaluated only in 'a synthetic benchmark environment' over 'controlled simulation trials', not in practice.

DynTaskMAS contributes orchestration across agents, dispatching ready tasks to available agents for parallelism (runner-up: planning_and_control_flow); throughput measured on self-built tasks vs sequential baselines.

Ablation 'demonstrates that Retrospective Reflection contributes most', so the revise-on-feedback step is the claim (runner-up: self_evolution); evidence is their own Sema-Sim simulator across seven strategies.
